newsitem.title: UK: Closing overseas stock market indices.
newsitem.headline: Closing overseas stock market indices.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - Britain's leading blue-chip index finished little changed after an earlier Wall Street-inspired rally reversed and dragged British stocks off their best levels, dealers said. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,762.4, up 3.9 points, or 0.08 percent.
FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index surged to its

seventh consecutive record closing high in market dealings, underpinned by the dollar rising to 1.76 marks in European dealings and higher German debt prices. The DAX-30 index closed at 4.055.86, up 49.46 points, or 1.23 percent. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,026.97, down 3.13 points, or 0.08 percent.

PARIS - Stocks rose, bolstered by record gains on Wall Street, but stocks closed off their highs as late weakness in the bond market and a huge sale of Alcatel Alsthom shares weighed on the market, brokers said. The CAC-40 index closed at 2.950.56, up 20.75 points, or 0.71 percent.

ZURICH - Stocks failed to maintain an early upward drive, snapping a four-day bull run to end lower as market heavyweights such as Novartis, UBS and Nestle turned negative on early Wall Street losses. The Swiss market index closed at 5,977.1, down 35.5 points, or 0.59 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks closed moderately lower as sentiment was hurt by doubts over Japan's economic recovery and concerns over the financial health of the nation's companies, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,697.17, down 156.72 points, or 0.79 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed lower after slipping into negative territory in the last half-hour of trade, chiefly on profit-taking in utilities, but brokers said the market would find support near current levels. The Hang Seng index closed at 14,703.73, down 88.44 points, or 0.60 percent.

SYDNEY - Stocks closed on a strong tone as gold stocks moved higher for the first time in four days and yield-sensitive stocks rose on hopes of another interest-rate cut. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,696.1, up 16.9 points or 0.63 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Stocks renewed their downward move as sentiment took a triple hit from the ongoing bullion price fall, a shaky rand and a poorly performing bond market, dealers said. The All-Share index closed at 7,299.2, down 11.1 points, or 0.15 percent. The All-Gold index closed at 905.3, down 18.4 points, or 1.99 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,759.3, down 7.0 points or 0.08 percent.
